angle: one detail at large scale, the rest implied by the frame's edge
subject: The eggbeater drill's face wheel seen huge and cropped: its hatched cast web and rim of lugs fill the left, the bright pinion sits on the lugs, and the spindle runs off the right edge into a chuck.
controls: ratio: the wheel grows against the pinion, its radius 150 to 300 px, so the rim's arc flattens from a tight curve to nearly straight while its right-most point stays put (shape of the rim and web outline).
teeth: lugs round the rim, 18 to 144 on the whole wheel, about 3 to 20 in view (count).
wear: each lug's corners round off, a crisp block at 0 to a worn lozenge at 100 (shape of the lug outlines).
bite: the pinion slides along the spindle from clear of the rim onto the lug ring, about 40 px of travel (position of the pinion node).
reference: library/theseus-tower/README.md; opxy/craft.md (hatching for a solid's mass, here the cast web)
risks: Hatching here is the drawing language for the cast web's mass, not a state; craft.md reserves hatching for semi-opaque or inactive regions, so the owner should say whether a hatched solid reads as 'there but not active'. Ratio reshapes the rim, web edge and every lug at once (one path plus many nodes repositioned): expensive on change. The visible lug count at teeth 3 is under three, and the frame's 20 % hatched area is the densest of the five (82 % black).
